comment.body: Thanks for the supplied startup evidence. @jiripolasek has already identified the missing System.Reactive dependency and requested a reinstall. Could you confirm the exact version installed afterward and whether PowerToys Run now starts? Please use the official installer for your existing installation scope and preserve your settings; do not download loose DLLs. If it still fails, report the new occurrence time. There is no need to re-upload the same ZIP or repeat the unrelated Copilot icon warning.

prerequisites: Disposable Windows test account and trusted matching installer.
Clean-install and in-place-update test environments; preserve original settings and installed-file evidence.
steps: Compare System.Reactive and the PowerLauncher dependency graph after clean install and update.
Start Run with input-delay settings on and off and record whether SetupSearchTextBoxReactiveness initializes.
In a disposable installation copy only, make the dependency unavailable and compare the resulting startup stack with the supplied FileNotFoundException.
reproduce.expected: Supported install/update paths deploy a resolvable System.Reactive assembly and Run starts without the recorded fatal exception.

fix_assessment.rationale: The fatal dependency-load path is established, but the installer/update/local-removal cause and corresponding correction require controlled validation.

proposed_fixes.title: Validate and preserve the Run System.Reactive deployment dependency
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Run startup requires System.Reactive, and the reported installation cannot resolve it. A missing or inconsistent deployed dependency is supported; an upstream packaging omission versus local removal is not yet proven.
verification: A clean installation and an in-place update both start Run with search-input delay enabled and disabled.
The installed System.Reactive identity resolves through the deployed dependency graph; an intentionally missing assembly reproduces the recorded exception in a disposable copy.
Verify the resulting installer/update, not only a developer build; ensure Program plugin icon warnings do not get misreported as this startup cause.

confidence.rationale: The current supplied fatal stack and required source dependency agree. Payload completeness and the mechanism that removed or omitted the assembly have not been independently measured.

plan: Compare the trusted0.102.3001 x64 installer payload and clean installation with an updated installation, checking System.Reactive identity and PowerLauncher dependency resolution.

Correct the demonstrated deployment path and add a release payload/dependency smoke check; retain a repair-install workaround only after verifying it, without deleting user settings or downloading loose DLLs.
